description.narrative: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$40 million and an additional co-investment envelope of up to US$30 million under the delegated authority framework, in Quadria Capital Fund III LP (the Fund or Fund III), a private equity fund dedicated to investments in the healthcare sector in South and Southeast Asia. The target Fund size is US$800 million (with a hard cap of US$1 billion). The Fund aims to provide equity to growth stage healthcare companies and will focus on strategic initiatives and operational improvements in its portfolio companies. The Fund will make investments in companies focused on the provision of healthcare delivery, life sciences, medical technology, and associated healthcare services. The Fund will be registered in the Singapore Islands as a limited partnership.

Stakeholders (Fund's portfolio companies) Increased access to private equity capital and value creation for health sector focused mid-market companies in India and Southeast Asia region: The main Project Outcomes include increased access to private equity capital and value creation for mid-market companies in the Indian and Southeast Asian health sector and their ability to improve customers or patient health outcomes. South and Southeast Asia have strong unmet demand for quality healthcare. Following the strategy of its previous funds, the Fund plans to invest in quality, scalable businesses that address the mass market at an affordable price on a financially sustainable basis, thereby improving access to quality, affordable healthcare across Asia.
Stakeholder (customers/patient health outcomes) Increased access to affordable and quality health products and services for investees' customers: Quadria invests in healthcare companies that generate positive development impacts, contributing to increases in the provision of health services and improved access to affordable and quality health products. Investments by previous funds (Fund I and Fund II) have led to an increase in patients served by 11 million among a total of 34 million patients served by the Fund investee companies. Many of the invested companies have provided their services and products with 40 to 50 percent discounts for local patients. Fund III will continue its investment strategy, selecting companies in which development impact is intrinsically linked to its business model.
Competitiveness Increasing competitiveness in the South and Southeast Asian health market by promoting alternate funding options and demonstrating the ongoing viability of a healthcare-focused PE model: The private health sector provides more than half of the health services in the region, easing capacity constraints of the public health sector. However, in response to increasing demand for health services, further investment is needed. PE funds provide an alternate source of capital that supports funding options for scaling health services. Since 2017, around $12 billion across 132 deals has been invested by PE funds in healthcare across India and Southeast Asia, representing around 10 percent of PE activity in the regions. IFC expects that Fund III will build on the signal sent by Fund II, encouraging other fund managers to raise funds and reduce the reliance on DFI investors.

name.narrative: Quadria Capital Investment Management Pte Ltd, the investment manager, is located in Singapore, and Quadria Capital Advisors Pvt Ltd, the investment advisor, is located in Delhi, India. The Funds investment and management team is located in those two locations. The Fund plans to invest across a number of developing countries in both South Asia and Southeast Asia, with an approximately even distribution across the two regions. Its current deal pipeline includes potential projects in both South and Southeast Asia.
